# Upper recheck — final_portability

Approve upper `4008f4984ad0e6fc26d7fd1c1e3d6ca28673cc41` for the portability/testing lens. I could not break this revision in the bounded checks below. All of my prior valid triple-literal, apostrophe, literal-ellipsis, and Unicode-control counterexamples now produce the intended results. Core fit: yes; these are stdlib-only, repository-local text checks without agent/provider-specific setup. My lower approval at `5a9f044f84fbcc21597f7bf44466cab9b3694b42` remains unchanged.

No correctness findings remain from this review. This verdict applies only to the exact pinned candidate, not to later changes or the parent's pending publication/CI gates.

## Prior failures and independent counterchecks

The four valid-Python triple-literal counterexamples now each produce one source advisory on both interpreters, including collapsed spaces in `'''Don't  change'''`, an omission inside that literal, a raw-prefixed triple, and embedded double quotes. Each changed quote is recognized as one complete literal span. Both source and altered quotation still pass `ast.parse`, so rejection is attributable to fidelity rather than malformed syntax.

The six prior apostrophe/code-whitespace probes all return their expected results on each interpreter. The three original false-literal-ellipsis probes receive advisories; raw U+13439 and `𓐹` continue to produce blocking frozen-record findings. All reproduction fixtures use real Git operations.

An additional independent matrix passes 240 of 240 comparisons on each interpreter, with zero skips. It combines single/double triple delimiters; plain, `r`, and `u` prefixes; embedded apostrophes, double quotes, Markdown emphasis, backticks, non-ASCII text, and newlines; plain/emphasized/inline-code presentation where applicable; exact values and one-space deletions. Both source programs parse as Python in every case. Exact values pass and altered literal whitespace fails.

## Exhaustive Unicode portability check

I independently derived the expected identifier and decimal sets from the actual Python 3.14.6 Unicode 16.0.0 database, then evaluated both production predicates for every one of the 1,114,112 code points on each interpreter. Python 3.9.6 and 3.14.6 agree exactly with that reference:

| Predicate | Selected/executed code points per interpreter | Accepted code points | Mismatches | Skips |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Identifier continuation | 1,114,112 / 1,114,112 | 145,620 | 0 | 0 |
| Decimal digit spelling | 1,114,112 / 1,114,112 | 760 | 0 | 0 |

On Python 3.9, the 10,132-code-point supplement also equals exactly the Unicode 16 continuation set minus the built-in Unicode 13 set: no missing or extra entries. The identifier-set SHA-256 is `1a926f28e20a43dac10e372f6171a68d894c2ab2a5f95d0ba7d81804ae2d3c64`; the decimal-set SHA-256 is `8ba14ca72eef061af8b9f8cf0ea40c3800edff0827bfd381c54229d6d65089c5`, identical across interpreters.

## Tests, discovery, and damaged controls

Both interpreters discover all 6 of 6 new methods. AST definitions, `unittest`, and shard selection each count 586 queue methods without duplicate names or skips; 16 test files are discovered.

The selected suite includes every source test, shard discovery, and the cheap input-ownership checks:

```text
Python 3.14.6: Ran 50 tests in 47.815s — OK; selected=50 executed=50 failures=0 errors=0 skips=0
Python 3.9.6:  Ran 50 tests in 49.949s — OK; selected=50 executed=50 failures=0 errors=0 skips=0
```

All six new methods turn red under relevant damaged controls on each interpreter. Short-quote-only matching gives 31 embedded-triple and 6 omission-boundary subtest failures. Refusing all quotes gives 38 exact-triple/escape-parity failures. Treating new visible symbols as identifier characters gives 20 failures; treating new identifier characters as separators gives 16; ASCII-only decimal matching gives 24. All 12 of 12 delta control runs fail by assertions, with no errors/skips.

The three original controls remain effective on both interpreters: accept-all-quotes produces 3 subtest failures, reading current working-tree bytes after capture produces 6, and Python `splitlines` for source selection produces 45. All 6 of 6 original control runs fail by assertions, with no errors/skips. Total: 18 of 18 expected-red control runs.

The runtime delta changes the quoted-string and number patterns plus `quote_identifier_continue`; their consumers remain within source comparison. `git diff --exit-code 5a9f044f84fbcc21597f7bf44466cab9b3694b42..HEAD -- automation/markdown_semantics.py` returns empty output/exit 0, preserving the lower shared-parser classification unchanged. The snapshot/path readers, lifecycle checks, hooks, and environment configuration have no runtime delta in this recheck.

## Exact reproduction commands and artifacts

For each actual interpreter, `python3` and `/usr/bin/python3`, I ran the following with environment `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 TMPDIR=/private/tmp/final-portability-upper-r4-fixtures`. Prepend that environment and interpreter to each line:

```text
/private/tmp/final-portability-targeted.py /private/tmp/agentfold-final-review-upper-r4 upper
/private/tmp/final-portability-upper-r3-confirm-triples.py /private/tmp/agentfold-final-review-upper-r4
/private/tmp/final-portability-upper-r2-probes.py /private/tmp/agentfold-final-review-upper-r4
/private/tmp/final-portability-probes.py /private/tmp/agentfold-final-review-upper-r4
/private/tmp/final-portability-discovery.py /private/tmp/agentfold-final-review-upper-r4 26d6b2b0afcf5cf251767bdec0adbd8d5cf6e611
/private/tmp/final-portability-upper-r4-controls.py /private/tmp/agentfold-final-review-upper-r4
/private/tmp/final-portability-controls.py /private/tmp/agentfold-final-review-upper-r4 upper
```

The two exhaustive commands ran sequentially; the first writes the independent reference set used by the second:

```text
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 /private/tmp/final-portability-upper-r4-unicode.py /private/tmp/agentfold-final-review-upper-r4 reference
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 /usr/bin/python3 /private/tmp/final-portability-upper-r4-unicode.py /private/tmp/agentfold-final-review-upper-r4 compare
```

The independent literal matrix ran with each interpreter and `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1`:

```text
/private/tmp/final-portability-upper-r4-literal-matrix.py /private/tmp/agentfold-final-review-upper-r4
```

Logs are `/private/tmp/final-portability-upper-r4-{tests,triple-probes,apostrophe-probes,original-probes,delta-controls,original-controls,unicode,literal-matrix}-{314,39}.log`. New scratch scripts/reference data use the same `final-portability-upper-r4-` prefix; old probes/reports are unchanged. Controls mutate only objects in their own test process.

Final clone status is empty with `git -c core.fsmonitor=false --no-optional-locks status --porcelain=v1`; `git diff --quiet --no-ext-diff` and `git diff --cached --quiet --no-ext-diff` both exit 0. `git rev-parse HEAD` remains `4008f4984ad0e6fc26d7fd1c1e3d6ca28673cc41`.

Limits: I did not duplicate the parent's full matrix, whole-history corpus, record-free projection, owner-preservation checks, hosted CI, or publication checks. The source checker deliberately recognizes lexical literal forms rather than inferring prose/code intent; the documented ambiguous-prefix limitation remains. Unicode assignments after 16.0 need an explicit data update. This review used only the mechanical inputs, permitted clone code/contracts/Git objects, and my own earlier evidence; no worker or other-reviewer verdicts. No clone/index/configuration or shared-record writes occurred. No confidence percentage was measured.
